name: Student Permission (Stamp 2) & Graduate Scheme (Stamp 1G)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires enrolment in a full-time course on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes (ILEP).
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission to an ILEP-listed course.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires proof of funds (commonly around €10,000/year) beyond tuition.

This requires graduating from an Irish Level 8 (bachelor's) or Level 9-10 (master's/doctorate) programme — Level 8 grants 12 months, Level 9-10 grants 24 months, full-time work without a permit (no self-employment).

outcome.duration_length: student: duration of course, max 7 years (Level 8) / 8 years (Level 9+); graduate scheme: 12 months (Level 8) or 24 months (Level 9-10)

sources.title: Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G) - Immigration Service Delivery

notes: Work rights during study (Stamp 2): 20 hours/week during term, 40 hours/week during scheduled holiday periods (June-September and 15 Dec-15 Jan) — a genuinely standardised holiday-period definition worth flagging, distinct from the more open-ended 'scheduled breaks' language used elsewhere in this dataset. Stamp 1G duration is genuinely tiered by credential level (12 months Level 8, 24 months Level 9-10) — a real and confirmed structural gradation, though it grants full-time work WITHOUT self-employment rights, a specific restriction worth noting. Direct feeder into ie_critical_skills_employment_permit and ie_general_employment_permit, closing Ireland's version of the core Journey chain seen throughout this dataset — time on this route is reckonable for eventual citizenship purposes, unlike some other countries where student time doesn't count toward naturalisation residence.
